bearings.paper_claim: Summed BISG posteriors (PSM) give lower absolute error than modal assignment (PM) in nearly all districts. In NC, PSM Black-share error never exceeds about 5 pp; in GA it peaks about 5 pp. PSM White-share error is near 0 in NC and reaches about 10 pp in GA.
bearings.paper_location: Lines 184-196 (district results); Abstract lines 17-20; Discussion lines 220-224. Item page labels are unreliable; cite lines.
bearings.system_side: engine.py lines 264-270 (categorical_map branch) compute mu = P @ m as the expected value and variance P @ (m*m) - mu^2 for estimated categorical fields. The draw spec in the same branch samples from the probability columns, not argmax.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper validates area-level aggregates of voter-level race posteriors for Black vs White in two segregated states. CUA is a person-level expected value for vendor consumer fields. Support for the person-level index is indirect and holds only where the class probabilities are roughly calibrated; calibration is the open ECE question.
bearings.verifier_note: Code claim holds as written. The paper's evidence concerns summed area aggregates, not person-level scores, so the support is an aggregation-rule analogy. The never-argmax PR2 rule is a brain claim that was not checked here.

bearings.paper_claim: Researchers should aggregate to a polygonal unit by summing estimated probabilities of racial membership. Assigning race to single voters makes errors drastically higher.
bearings.system_side: areas.py eb_top10_params (lines 435-449): area top-decile share is np.bincount of summed P(top10) contributions divided by row count (line 438), followed by beta-binomial EB shrinkage with a design-effect variance (lines 444-448).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The summed-probability step matches the paper's recommended aggregation. The paper does not test EB shrinkage or top-decile shares, so it says nothing about the shrinkage layer. Its expectation of larger error in heterogeneous areas is where shrinkage matters most. This is an analogy for the aggregation choice, not a validation of Terrier area values.
bearings.verifier_note: Both sides hold as written. The quoted phrase drastically higher is verbatim at line 222. Keep only as support for the aggregation rule.

bearings.paper_claim: Modal assignment gives a longer right tail of precinct error for White voters and higher district error than summed probabilities in nearly all simulated districts. For Black voters, PSM vastly outperforms PM at precinct level.
bearings.system_side: models.py lines 386-393 score Luna candidates by argmax accuracy against a modal majority baseline (confirmed). measures.py lines 197-220 count literal codes with raw.eq(code) over valid-code denominators (confirmed). The step that fills each blank with the most probable class was not located in the lines read. The 78 percent majority baseline was not found in the code.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies only if modal-filled codes reach an area-level share. Whether the v3 ingest reads the Luna-completed file remains unconfirmed. The rare-class under-count is a hypothesis; the paper measures bias for race only, not for vendor consumer fields.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper claim as written misattributes the longer right tail to Black voters. The text gives that finding for White voters (line 153), and a large PSM advantage for Black voters (line 154). Code side confirms argmax scoring and raw.eq counting, but not the modal-fill step or the 78 percent figure.
